newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Hyundai Motor paralysed by strike.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Hyundai Motor paralysed by strike.

text.p: Union workers at Hyundai Motor Co factories walked out on strike on Thursday, halting production at South Korea's largest carmaker, according to union and company officials.
The strike at the main plant in the south-eastern city of Ulsan and at a smaller production facility in the western city of Chonju began at 1 p.m. (0400 GMT).
"All lines are down," said a union official in Ulsan. The stoppage was confirmed by an official in the company's public relations department.

About 28,000 of the 35,000 workers at the Ulsan plant are members of a union affiliated with the outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions, which called a strike by all its 500,000 members in protest at the passage of a new labour law on Thursday.
Unions say the law threatens job security by allowing worker layoffs and flexible work hours.
